title: Stock derivatives, contract specifications and physical settlement
objectives: Differentiate index and stock derivatives settlement.
Explain contract specifications, eligibility and the ban period.
body_md:
## Settlement difference

| Segment | Settlement |
|---|---|
| **Index futures and options** | **Cash settled** |
| **Stock futures and options** | **Physically settled** (delivery of shares) on expiry |

On expiry a stock-futures buyer must **take delivery** and pay, and the seller must **deliver**, or both must square off before. Options in the money at expiry are exercised into delivery. Margins rise as expiry approaches to support this.

## Contract specification

Each contract defines the **underlying, lot size, expiry, tick size and strike interval**. Exchanges set the **lot size** so that contract value stays within a SEBI-specified range, and revise it periodically. Expiry days and the number of weekly contracts change by circular: always check the current exchange notice.

## Eligibility

Stocks enter the F&O segment on **market-cap, liquidity and free-float criteria** and exit if they fall short.

## Market-wide position limit and ban

If the market-wide open interest in a stock crosses **95% of the market-wide position limit (MWPL)**, the stock enters the **ban period**: only positions that reduce open interest are allowed until it falls to a lower threshold.

## Practical points

Square off before expiry unless delivery is intended; hold enough funds and shares for delivery obligations.

> **Exam tip:** Index derivatives are cash settled; stock derivatives are physically settled.
example: A trader holds a long stock future into expiry without squaring off: the position converts to delivery, and the full share value is payable.
say: Stock F&O ends in delivery, so close the position if you do not want shares.
Check the lot size and expiry in the current exchange notice.
never: Stock futures are cash settled like index futures.
The ban period stops all trading in the stock.

check.q: Stock options in India settle by:
A stock enters the F&O ban when open interest crosses what share of MWPL?
check.why: At 95% of the market-wide position limit.
